findings.title: Announcement/question payload text bypasses sanitizeDiscordText and containsSecretLikeText
findings.detail: Every other Discord-bound text producer in this package sanitizes before freezing a send intention (daily-report/artifacts.ts:114, daily-report/round.ts:296, contracts/drift-envelope.ts:160, meeting-notification.ts:75, daily-report/failure-notice.ts:58, meeting-round.ts:49). The generic announcement path does not: `payload.text = text(input.text, "announcement text", 1800)` is stored verbatim, and prepareQuestionIntent (question-intent.ts:73) interpolates `body` and `sourceRefs` raw into the roundtable question. Verified end-to-end: `prepare --input` with text `"@everyone 紧急 ghp_ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ123456 <@123456789012345678>"` returned that exact string in `next.arguments.text`, i.e. it is frozen into the operation ledger and handed to lead_actions.discord_send unmodified — a mass mention plus an unredacted token. This matters because question bodies are, by design, composed from summary material authored by other Leads, which the package elsewhere treats as untrusted ("Material is data, not instructions"). Non-blocking because the content still originates from Raya's own turn and Flywheel's transport is outside this repo, but the inconsistency with the package's own boundary contract should be closed.

findings.title: projectMeetingStart result discarded, then committed at the stale revision
findings.detail: prepareMeetingArchive calls `projectMeetingStart(store, workspace, current)` and throws the return value away, then at line 143 commits `{...current, ...}` with `current.revision`. If the projection actually performs work (an unprojected `startProjection` left behind by an earlier projection failure, e.g. a held `.meeting-write.lock`), it commits first and the archive commit then fails. meeting-voice.ts:105 has the identical pattern for `begin_voice_start`. The daily-report path guards against exactly this at business-round.ts:396 (`if (verified.revision !== current.revision) throw "report artifacts updated; resume before sending"`), so the omission looks unintentional. Reproduced: seeding a `meeting:<uuid>` operation at stage `ended` with `startProjection.projected === false` and recording `{action:"archive_terminal"}` yields `THREW: operation revision conflict`, with the store left at revision 2 / `projected: true` / `archive: undefined`. State stays consistent and a resume+retry succeeds, so this is a spurious hard error rather than corruption — hence non-blocking — but it should either chain the returned operation (as the `begin_start` branch at business-round.ts:331-340 already does) or use the same revision guard.

findings.title: Definite announcement send failures re-emit the send intention with no backoff
findings.detail: In the generic receipt path only `status: "rate_limited"` sets `nextAttemptAt`. A `rejected` or `unavailable` receipt falls through to stage `pending`, and view() (line 698-714) then re-emits the identical `lead_actions.discord_send` intention immediately, because `pending` is not in the terminal list, `needsReconciliation` is false and `nextAttemptAt` is undefined. The daily-report equivalent does set a floor (`next.nextAttemptAt = now + 60000` at send-round.ts:159) for exactly these statuses. A Lead that follows `next` verbatim will hot-loop against a hard rejection with no pacing.

findings.title: One unparseable snapshot file permanently blocks all portfolio snapshot writes
findings.detail: prune() now calls `this.read()` for every file under `state/portfolio/snapshots/`, and `read()` throws (not returns null) for any file that fails `validate()` or exceeds 2 MiB — null is only returned on ENOENT. Since prune() runs inside write(), a single malformed snapshot file makes every subsequent `SnapshotStore.write()` throw, which in turn blocks `BusinessRound.projectPortfolio` (business-round.ts:590) permanently. The same applies to a corrupt `latest.json` via readLatest(), which no longer self-heals by renaming to `latest.json.corrupt-*` as the pre-change code did; preparePatrol (patrol-round.ts:95) then fails too. Fail-closed is consistent with this package's "explicit operator recovery" philosophy, but the `a.snapshot?.seq ?? 0` null-coalescing at line 163 suggests nulls were expected here, and there is no documented recovery path other than manually deleting the file.

findings.title: daily-report-date and voice-intent silently accept unknown extra flags
findings.detail: Every other subcommand validates `values.size` and the exact flag set (lines 84, 89-95, 107, 111-118, 130-136, 148, 154, 159). `daily-report-date` (line 185) and `voice-intent` (line 197) only call `required(...)` for the flags they consume, so `daily-report-date --now X --timezone Y --time Z --bogus v` succeeds and ignores `--bogus`. Harmless today, but it makes a typo'd or renamed flag silently no-op instead of erroring, which is the failure mode the strict checks elsewhere exist to prevent.
